subject: traditional2mirt() output for more than 4 categories?

messages.author: 6855b04443295af7
messages.subject: traditional2mirt() output for more than 4 categories?
parts:
Hello Phil, 

I used the traditional2mirt() to convert the classical IRT parameterisation to slope-intercepts, and then convert it back to the classical IRT params to see if they were identical. 
And they are if the categories are no more than 4. I tried it with 5 categories but the returned values of the last parameter (b5) is different. 

Is this expected? If so, can I assume that the object from generate.mirt_object() is using the appropriate slope-intercept values that I provided using the classical IRT params?

Reproducible code is below. 

Many thanks,
Aiden

====================
itempar2=matrix(c(1,  0.70, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1, -0.27, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1,  0.60, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1, -0.22, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1, -0.08, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1, -0.14, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1, -1.13, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1, -0.03, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1,  1.10, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87,
                  1,  0.08, -1.81, -0.4, 0.34, 1.87), ncol=6, byrow=TRUE)
colnames(itempar2) = c('a', 'b1', 'b2', 'b3', 'b4', 'b5')



# convert to slope-intercepts
a_slopeint = NULL
(ncat=ncol(itempar2))
for(i in 1:nrow(itempar2)){
  vec=as.numeric(itempar2[i,])
  slopeint <- traditional2mirt(vec, 'gpcm', ncat=ncat)
  a_slopeint =rbind(a_slopeint, slopeint)
}

# generate mirt object based on IRT model used to calibrate item
obj =generate.mirt_object(parameters = a_slopeint, itemtype = 'gpcm')
coef(obj, simplify= TRUE, IRTpar=TRUE)

output
$items
            a    b1     b2     b3   b4   b5
Item.1  1  0.70 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 1.17
Item.2  1 -0.27 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 2.14
Item.3  1  0.60 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 1.27
Item.4  1 -0.22 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 2.09
Item.5  1 -0.08 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 1.95
Item.6  1 -0.14 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 2.01
Item.7  1 -1.13 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 3.00
Item.8  1 -0.03 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 1.90
Item.9  1  1.10 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 0.77
Item.10 1  0.08 -1.81 -0.4 0.34 1.79

parts:
Thanks, it looks like the math wasn't tested for gpcms with more than 5 categories so I never noticed this coding error. Fix is on the dev version, and your example is now correctly back translatable.

Phil
